notes: Low, hot vineyards, such as along the southern Mediterranean coast, give grapes high in alcohol and low in acidity.
Oak aging has a long tradition in Spain.
Cariñena reds have the style of Garnacha from a hot climate.
Its young whites and rosés are best drunk within the year.
Sherry is made mainly from Palomino, and because it is fortified after fermentation, most sherry is dry.
Fino and Manzanilla are light, very dry and delicate, while Amontillado and Oloroso are darker and heavier from aging with air.
Amontillado is dry and nutty, and Oloroso is full bodied, complex and round.
Palo Cortado combines the nose of Amontillado with the depth and body of Oloroso.
Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel, from dried grapes, are intensely sweet, and Cream sherry is usually Oloroso sweetened with Pedro Ximénez.
Priorat is dense, rich, concentrated and dark, with noticeable tannin.
It shows dark black fruit with notes of fig and tar.
Tempranillo and Garnacha make Ribera del Duero's full-bodied reds.
Oak aging gives Rioja reds pronounced vanilla flavors, long a trademark of the region, though some modern producers use less oak.
Tempranillo has a fairly neutral profile, so in Rioja it is often blended or aged long in oak, where it takes on the barrel's flavor.

Rioja Alta gives wines with body and high acidity suited to barrel aging, Alavesa slightly higher alcohol and a little less acidity, and Oriental, the warmest and driest zone, riper wines suited to blending.
Some white Rioja Reserva and Gran Reserva ages for decades into a highly distinctive, aromatic wine.
Moscatel de Valencia is a sweet fortified wine made only from Muscat of Alexandria, with wine spirit added to the must.
Navarra has a long rosado tradition, mostly from Garnacha and made by the bleeding method.
Valdepeñas has long been known for clarete, made by mixing white and red grapes.
Rías Baixas Albariño has complex aromas of citrus, flowers and fruit, with apple standing out.
On the palate it is balanced and fresh, with good structure, some richness and a floral, fruity finish.
Poor, sandy soils and a ripening season of modest sunshine and moderate temperatures give wines known more for their acidity and aroma than their alcohol.
Barrel-aged whites add toast, smoke, vanilla and nutty notes.
The reds are light in body and moderately tannic, with red berry and herbal aromas.
The reds smell of red and black fruit and violets, and taste fresh, with medium to full body.
The whites show white and stone fruit, citrus and white flowers, with freshness and medium to full body.
Barrel-aged reds add vanilla, coconut, toast and spice.
Very cold winters, long sunny days and extreme temperatures give wines with structure and high alcohol.
The reds show red and black fruit, with medium to full body and balanced alcohol and acidity.
Barrel-aged reds, from Roble to Gran Reserva, add oak aromas as they age.
The whites are light in body, with fruity, floral or herbal aromas and medium to fairly high acidity.
Young reds are deep cherry to garnet, fruity, fleshy and balanced, with soft tannin and a long finish.
Rosés are strawberry to raspberry pink, intensely floral and fruity, fresh and powerful.
Calatayud Superior is a deep red, with fruit, balsamic, mineral, toast and spice aromas.
In Crianza reds, tannins firm in youth round out in bottle.
It gives broad, fleshy wines with good alcohol and acidity, ripe fruit and well-integrated tannin.
The reds run from violet to brick red, with red and black fruit, and are tannic.
Other grapes add color stability, acidity and aging potential.
Sweet and fortified Monastrell wines add dried fruit notes.
Yecla's very dry climate, arid soils and strong sun give Monastrell wines of good color and high alcohol.
Reds are traditionally made from old Monastrell vines, very rich in tannin.
They are fruity, fleshy and warm, tannic yet smooth, balanced and concentrated.
Rosés are raspberry to cherry pink, fresh and strongly fruity.
More than 3,000 hours of sun a year ripen La Mancha's grapes to wines of 11 to 14% alcohol, with balanced acidity.
Its soils suit full-bodied, high-alcohol reds that are good for aging.
Young reds are violet to garnet, fruity and tannic, with alcohol and acidity in balance.
Young dry whites are greenish to yellow, fruity and lightly acidic.
Gran Reserva reds show toast and vanilla.
Catalunya wines have attractive color, medium to high aromatic intensity, moderate acidity and good alcohol.
Young whites and rosés are fruity or floral, light and fresh.
Young reds are clearly fruity, and barrel aging adds vanilla, toast and spice and makes them rounder.
Fortified wines are warm and unctuous, and aged ones gain nutty notes.
Young whites are fresh and fruity, with real presence on the palate.
Rosés are fresh, with red fruit, and those from Prieto Picudo have notable body.
In León and Fermoselle, whole bunches added during fermentation give rosés deeper color and a light sparkle.
